name: Boids
description: Craig Reynolds's 1987 artificial life program that simulates the flocking behaviour of birds (boids) using three simple steering rules: separation, alignment, and cohesion. Boids is a foundational demonstration that realistic collective motion emerges from local individual rules without centralised control.
reputation: Seminal work in computer graphics and artificial life; widely taught and replicated as a canonical example of emergence from simple rules.
notes: Original algorithm is simple and widely reimplemented; no canonical codebase or benchmark scoring. Primarily used for education and visualisation.
